CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's fundamental health is strong with excellent revenue growth (+22.2% YoY in Q1 2026), robust margins (16.5% operating margin, 13.3% net margin), and a record $62.7B backlog providing multi-year revenue visibility. However, the valuation has become extremely stretched and disconnected from the company's cyclical industrial nature. The stock trades at a P/E of 47.6x (vs. 18.8x a year ago), P/B of 24.1x (vs. 10.3x a year ago), and an earnings yield of just 2.1% - all at or near the top of their 365-day ranges. This represents a 150%+ P/E expansion that has far outpaced the 22% revenue growth and 30% EPS growth. The stock has surged 31.9% in the last quarter alone and 148% over the past year, driven by AI data center narrative rather than fundamental re-rating. Michael Burry's high-profile short position at $1,060.98 citing unsustainable price-to-sales ratios at 30-year highs adds a credible near-term catalyst for multiple compression. Additionally, tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B projected for 2026 are constraining margins near the lower end of targets, Resource Industries segment margins have contracted 700bps, and the stock was dropped from several Russell style indices triggering passive outflows. The combination of extreme valuation, deteriorating margin trends in core segments, and a high-profile bearish catalyst creates a compelling case for significant downside risk.
